1_trimethoprim_selectivity.title: Inhibitor binding analysis of dihydrofolate reductases from various species
1_trimethoprim_selectivity.note: Confirmed via PubMed esummary (PMID 4378654, Mol Pharmacol 1965 Sep;1(2):126-36) and CrossRef (same title/volume/pages; DOI resolves live to a ScienceDirect/Elsevier page — Molecular Pharmacology's back catalog was retroactively assigned Elsevier DOIs). This is the classic Hitchings-lab paper comparing inhibitor (including trimethoprim) binding constants for DHFR from E. coli, S. aureus, P. vulgaris vs. vertebrate (rat liver) enzyme, which underlies the widely-cited ~10^4-10^5-fold bacterial-vs-mammalian selectivity figure for trimethoprim. CAVEAT: I could not confirm the literal numeral '10^4-10^5-fold' appears verbatim in this 1965 paper itself — that rounded figure is how later reviews summarize the Ki/Ki ratios reported here and in follow-on Hitchings-era work. Cite this as the primary data source; if the paper text is quoted for the exact fold-number, verify the number against the original text/a review before print.

2_methotrexate_not_selective.title: Inhibitor binding analysis of dihydrofolate reductases from various species
2_methotrexate_not_selective.note: Same paper as item 1 (verified identically). This study is also the standard primary source for methotrexate's lack of bacterial/vertebrate DHFR selectivity relative to trimethoprim — it reports methotrexate as a potent inhibitor across bacterial and vertebrate DHFRs alike, in contrast to trimethoprim's steep species differential. No separate methotrexate-specific cross-species paper was located that is more directly on-point than this one; if the paper needs a distinct citation from item 1, consider a modern review instead (e.g. Schweitzer/Dicker/Bertino 1990, item 5) rather than fabricating a second primary source.

3_pyrimethamine_selectivity_plasmodium.authors: Yuthavong Y, Tarnchompoo B, Vilaivan T, Chitnumsub P, Kamchonwongpaisan S, Charman SA, McLennan DN, White KL, Vivas L, Bongard E, Thongphanchang C, Taweechai S, Vanichtanankul J, Rattanajak R, Arwon U, Fantauzzi P, Yuvaniyama J, Charman WN, Matthews D
3_pyrimethamine_selectivity_plasmodium.title: Malarial dihydrofolate reductase as a paradigm for drug development against a resistance-compromised target
3_pyrimethamine_selectivity_plasmodium.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 109(42):16823-16828
3_pyrimethamine_selectivity_plasmodium.note: Confirmed via PubMed esummary (PMID 23035243, PNAS 2012 Oct 16;109(42):16823-8). Provides the residue-level basis for antifolate (pyrimethamine-class / P218) selectivity for Plasmodium DHFR over human DHFR, centered on conserved Arg122 in the parasite enzyme and three species-divergent residues near it in the human enzyme. A companion structural reference is Kongsaeree et al. 2005 PNAS (item below / PDB 2BL9), which is the P. vivax DHFR-pyrimethamine crystal structure paper — cite together if both binding-affinity selectivity and structural/residue detail are needed.

4_saureus_F98Y_resistance.authors: Dale GE, Broger C, D'Arcy A, Hartman PG, DeHoogt R, Jolidon S, Kompis I, Labhardt AM, Langen H, Locher H, Page MG, Stüber D, Then RL, Wipf B, Oefner C
4_saureus_F98Y_resistance.title: A single amino acid substitution in Staphylococcus aureus dihydrofolate reductase determines trimethoprim resistance
4_saureus_F98Y_resistance.note: Confirmed via PubMed esummary (PMID 9054967, J Mol Biol 1997 Feb 14;266(1):23-30, DOI 10.1006/jmbi.1996.0770). This is exactly the canonical F98Y (Phe98->Tyr98) trimethoprim-resistance mechanism paper — determined ternary crystal structures of wild-type S. aureus DHFR (with MTX and TMP/NADPH) and the F98Y mutant. NOTE: none of the 8 PDB IDs the user asked me to verify (7NAE/2W3A/2W9H/2BL9/4M6K/1RG7/1U72/6P9Z) is actually this paper's F98Y mutant structure or its associated PDB entries — 2W9H and 6P9Z in the requested list are both WILD-TYPE S. aureus DHFR. If a PDB structure of the F98Y mutant itself is needed for a figure, that is a separate entry (e.g. PDB 3M09, seen in search results as 'F98Y TMP-resistant Dihydrofolate Reductase from Staphylococcus aureus') and was NOT in the requested list, so I have not verified it — flag this to the user before using it.
